1973.websynth.zip: A project bundle, so its sampled parts travel inside the file.
First_Light.websynth.json: One riff, four chords: the whole progression is bar transposes on two banks. POLY filter, hat choke, tempo-locked LFO — and the arp is armed, so hold a key.
Gankogui.websynth.json: Twelve-eight, and three lanes on three different cycles: the bell locked to the 24-tick bar, the riff looping every 16 ticks and the motion lane every 18. The whole machine only lands together once every six bars.
Nocturne.websynth.json: The long, slow one: four sequencer tracks through the POLY filter, with motion driving it.
Right.websynth.json: No drums anywhere — four sequencer tracks and motion carry the whole piece.
Run_Away_2.websynth.zip: The Run Away idea rebuilt as a project bundle, sampled parts alongside the synth.
Slouch.websynth.json: Swing sits at zero — every bit of the drag is per-step micro-timing. The snare is five notches late, the clap trails it by another two, the kick pushes ahead, and one hi-hat lands a third of a step off.
Tosti.websynth.json: Three sequencer tracks over a conga-and-clave kit.
Maison.websynth.json: French house, built around the ducker: the kick keys it, everything else breathes. Two bars of silence, a filter riser, then the drop. Mute the drum lane and the pumping stops with it.
Sweet_Dreams.websynth.json: The sequencer runs at 1/8 over all 16 cells, so every bank holds two bars — the riff and the vocal line each fit one bank, which is how eight banks cover the whole song. Four POLY tracks: bass, both riff lines and the melody or chord on top.
Blue_Monday.websynth.json: Two four-bar halves: the pulsing sequence with its two out-of-phase lines, and the octave bass under the hook and the melody. The drums carry the breaks — the kick roll, the dotted stop, a 32nd-note kick ratchet and the snare-and-clap rolls — over bars where the sequencer rests.
Around_the_World.websynth.json: The four sequencer tracks are the four instruments of the video — bass, the vocal, the guitar riff and the synth — playing one four-bar phrase, and motion lanes on the track mutes bring each part in and out, so the whole arrangement lives in the Motion card. Swing is at 27% for the lazy late 16ths of the pickups.
Take_on_Me.websynth.json: All sixteen banks, two bars each: the sequencer runs at 1/8 over 16 cells, so the intro, riff, verse, chorus and outro each fit as the arrangement's own bars rather than look-alikes. Each part keeps its own track — bass, the riff (brass in the chorus), the guitar's eighths and the strings or aahs on top — and the pad pulses in eighths because a held note would retrigger.
Running_Up_That_Hill.websynth.json: The drums are the song: a deep tom pattern in sixteenths, a kick on one and three and the crack on two and four, with a shaker and a clave standing in for the cabasa and woodblock. Over it, four tracks at 1/8 — bass, the hook, the strings' counter-line and the chord's top voice — each struck once and carried by a long release rather than held.
Eleanor_Rigby-1.websynth.json: Half of a pair: load Eleanor Rigby-2 on a second device, pair them over WiFi sync or MIDI and press Play on either one. This half is the low strings and the voice: the tune, the cello, the viola's lines and the second voice in the "Ah" sections. Its last verse has its own cello arpeggios, the cello doubling the tune and the A minor near the end. It plays complete on its own too.
Eleanor_Rigby-2.websynth.json: Half of a pair: load Eleanor Rigby-1 on a second device, pair them over WiFi sync or MIDI and press Play on either one. This half is the violins: the same tune, the staccato chord stabs and a pizzicato root under each stab, so it has a bass line when it plays alone. In the last chorus it switches to the "Ah, look at all the lonely people" line while the other device carries the chorus, as on the record.
1985-1.websynth.json: Half of a pair, Crockett's Theme: load 1985-2 on a second device, pair them over WiFi sync or MIDI and press Play on either one. This half is the groove: the octave bass pulse, the lead, the bridge guitar stabs and the drum kit. One patch plays both bass and lead, and velocity decides which one you hear: the filter envelope is negative, so a hard-hit note starts open and snaps shut, which is the bass pluck, while the soft lead barely closes and stays bright. With sustain at 1, a tied note is already where its envelopes are heading, so it holds without re-plucking. A motion lane mutes the lead through the opening progression. It plays complete on its own too.
1985-2.websynth.json: Half of a pair, Crockett's Theme: load 1985-1 on a second device, pair them over WiFi sync or MIDI and press Play on either one. This half is the strings and the same lead, over a percussion kit of cowbell, shakers, congas, bongo and clave. The sequencer runs at 1/8 over 16 cells, two bars a bank. The strings are a root and two inner voices, struck on the beat and held with ties. The swell into each verse is one held chord whose velocity climbs step by step. In the last verse the fourth track drops its string and doubles the lead an octave up. It plays complete on its own too.
